title: A letter from Wilno, 11 July 1757, on subsidies and the Strutyński affair (AGAD 1/338/0/1/131): read in part with the key of letter 446 by Prabal Gupta

steps.what: Claude Opus 5.5 transcribed the letter from the five scans; a blind GPT-6.1 Sol pass agreed on 88% of 2,514 tokens; the hard lines were re-read on enlarged images; about 300 differences are not settled on the scan.
The key of letter 446 (target branicki1757) was applied with no change and read French; a count-matching fit on this letter alone gives the same key for 97.7% of letter tokens (contributor's figure).

The decryption was read as French inside clear Polish: about 25 of some 460 cipher words doubtful or holding an unread code; the group 190 and three signs stay unread; a blind reader named the cipher text French and three controls noise.
The contributor searched the ledger, the card and scans of the unit and compared letters 446, 1398, 1399 and 1400; Konopczyński (1909) and Matuszewicz's memoirs tell the affair but not this letter.

Project check: an own script applied the reciprocal key to the 64 cipher lines and got the contributor's decryption in 62 lines and at 99.9% letter agreement; a word-list test gives 46.3% of letters in listed words against a mean of 4.5% and a best of 19.1% for 200 shuffled keys (VERIFICATION.md). No scan compared.

validation.notes: The key is that of letter 446 applied unchanged; a word-list test against 200 shuffled keys was used instead of the project's n-gram test (VERIFICATION.md).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: A sibling letter's key (letter 446, target branicki1757, the contributor's own) was applied unchanged and read French; the contributor's count-matching fit on this letter alone gives the same key for 97.7% of tokens (his figure). The project verified that the key decrypts the cipher lines into French and re-ran a shuffled-key control, but did not repeat the fit or see the scans.

texts.label: Letter from Wilno, 11 July 1757 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/131)
texts.summary: An unsigned letter from Wilno of 11 July 1757 to a patron in the Branicki circle, in the contributor's reading: the Castellan of Brest and Count Pociej, Strażnik of Lithuania, ask protection and a subsidy for the coming Lithuanian Tribunal, having borrowed up to two hundred thousand francs beyond the French subsidy; the Castellan's nephew Ciechanowiecki's memorial is to go to the French ambassador, the Count de L'Hôpital; in the contributor's reading Strutyński, Starost of Szakinów, came armed to the Brasław dietine to kill a Ciechanowiecki (the word 'massacre' is a conjecture) and is shielded by Field Marshal Apraksin. The identities of writer and addressee and the two rumours at the end are the contributor's inference.

reading_review.note: Read the contributor's French and Polish as clauses: the clauses build coherent sentences with holes at unread codes and doubtful words; the names and events are the contributor's reading, not an edition.

prior.where: The ledger gives no reading; the contributor searched the ledger, the card and scans of the unit, and compared four sibling letters; Konopczyński (1909) and Matuszewicz's memoirs tell the affair but do not give this letter on the pages cited.

human: Prabal Gupta set the task and directed the work (issue #331, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757); AI models (Claude, GPT) made the transcription passes and the reading. The key is his own key for letter 446. The project re-ran the decryption and a shuffled-key control; it has not seen the scans.
